chapter: The levee club and the St. Louis scene
title: The hungry stranger and the rough club owned by Green
summary: The man only wanted food. Thomas fed him at the club, where Green owned the place, Julia cooked spaghetti, and the band moved the piano out from the wall for fights.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Yeah but what happened to this guy who picked you up?
I'm giving you the whole picture.
Oh, this is all involved with this?
Oh, yes. Sims, at that time, was taking telegrams around.
Oh, yes, telegraph boy.

So, we got to talking about it one day. I sort of ran into him you know. And so he took the telegrams around and the guy would say, "So read it." These fellows couldn't read. "So read it." If it was bad news, out of nowhere comes bring him in the house two hands and they grabbed him and beat the shit out of him. didn't want the money, he So on a similar situation, this fellow -- he/... was hungry. So I took him to the club with me. And Julia, remember Julia?
Yeah. Well, he didn't really want your money?
No. He was hungry. He wanted food.
But he just picked you up just to sort of half scare you?
He had the right one because I was scared. And I figured I could outrun anybody. Damn near Jesse Owens.
JT (2 of 1) 57
Well, he was a great big fellow, I take it?

Yeah, but not only that, I mean the way he picked me up. I was strong, too. But, he wanted food. So I took him to the club. So Green, the guy who owned the joint, said, "Who is this?" I said, "A friend of mine." I mean, he's the owner of the club. (...) and at that time, they were serving food -- she was a tremendous cook -- Italian spaghetti at $1 a plate. So I took him upstairs and I said, "Well, Green, this your boy. ... Got him some food. I loved the band. I thought we had a helluva old band. I thought so. Laurence Madison, Tommy ... so we had to see what ... There were no guns there. Guys would come in, bad guys. Take the piano out and set it out from the wall. See the piano set -- see where you sitting -- so we take the piano and turn the piano around but the drummer was smart. Because he's going to be the first one to get in there when the fight starts behind the piano.
Oh, I see. You moved the piano out for protection.
Oh, what else, man.
That was really a rough area.

It was pretty rugged but they had some other things ... So, in the meantime, every night he thought he was protecting me, this same guy, and he wouldn't wait until I'd come out. He'd be standing on the corner.
JT (2 of 1) 58
He'd go down with you.
Oh, yeah. I told him, I told Julia, I said, after I'd got to know him, say hello to him, if anything goes wrong, Julia and Julia liked the idea. She's cooking. What the Hell.
Well, what did this guy do?
I don't know. I never asked him.
Oh, you never asked him.
That's his business, not mine.
